newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador raises banana prices, strike ends.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador raises banana prices, strike ends.

text.p: Ecuadorean banana producers ended a day-old strike Tuesday after the government raised official prices for the fruit.
Banana producer representatives signed an agreement with government officials to end their strike.
"I want to stress that the government is determined that this agreement will be respected," said Agriculture Minister Alfredo Saltos.
The government raised the official low season price range for a case of bananas to $3.60 and $4.20. In the high season, the minimum price will be $4.20.
Producers went on strike Monday after the government fixed a price of $4.20 per premium box, and $3.40 for extra quality.

Angry demonstrators blocked major highways with burning tires and dumping loads of bananas on roads. In the most serious incident, a demonstrating banana producer shot two people who tried to pass a roadblock.
Ecuador is the world's largest banana producer.
